category_title: High-achieving bilingual Latino fifth-graders who disassociate from academic labels through mischievous behaviors
minimal_context: The student is working independently on a practice reading passage about elephants and its corresponding questions.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent practice. Please read the passage about the elephant and complete the corresponding questions.

STUDENT: (Taps pencil rapidly on the desk) I'm already done with it.

TUTOR: That was very fast. Did you read the entire passage?

STUDENT: No, I just read paragraph one and two on the elephant. Then I saw the questions and then—um—it said paragraph six. So I just went to paragraph six.

TUTOR: You need to read every paragraph to prepare for the TAKS test. Please sit still and read it again.

STUDENT: (Starts stomping his feet, then stands up and begins walking around the room) I'm not doing that. I don't want to be a schoolboy kissing up to the teacher just to get a lot of good scores.

options.A: Affirm academic success in a way that does not single the student out from peers, and integrate his funds of knowledge into the reading curriculum.
options.B: Place an exclusive display board in the classroom only for the student to display his completed reading passages and corresponding questions.
options.C: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) at the end of each reading practice period.
options.D: Provide continuous, increasing amounts of reading passage practice work ("more work and more work") throughout the independent work time.
